title: Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services

reading.body:
This is a case of impersonation at scale, in which AI-generated video and text were used to create false identities of a real attorney and deploy them across social media platforms. The system had no human intermediary and no verification step. Scammers generated hundreds of fake accounts with AI content, directed victims to messaging apps, and collected payment for services never rendered. The deployment was criminal and the targets were people in a vulnerable legal position who had reason to trust the impersonated identity.

What would have caught this: platform verification of attorney accounts before monetization or service solicitation, human review of video content before posting, and detection systems tuned to flag repeated impersonation of the same real person across multiple accounts. The scale of the fraud, nearly 6,500 fake accounts, suggests the platforms' automated defenses did not flag either the impersonation pattern or the coordinated account creation.

It is not established how the scammers obtained training material or what specific AI tools they used to generate the videos. It is also not established whether the platforms were notified before the anti-piracy company's removals or whether they assisted in the investigation.

reports.title: Scammers steal identity of renowned Miami attorney to target immigrants on social media
South Florida immigration attorney says AI scammers are using his identity to target immigrants
Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services
Legal resident loses thousands seeking citizenship to AI immigration attorney

summary:
Angel Leal, a South Florida immigration attorney with over 30 years of experience, has become the target of sophisticated AI scams targeting vulnerable immigrants. Criminals have created hundreds of fake social media profiles and AI-generated videos depicting Leal offering immigration services he never provides, charging fees like $2,200 for fraudulent residency assistance. The fraud escalated dramatically in recent months, prompting Leal's office to hire an anti-piracy company that has removed nearly 6,500 fake accounts across platforms, including 3,500 on TikTok, 2,400 on Facebook, and 544 on Instagram.

The scams typically begin with social media videos directing victims to contact a phone number via WhatsApp, where perpetrators send phony contracts and falsely claim to help with legal status or immigration detention releases. Leal has changed his personal phone number and plans to contact local and federal authorities to investigate. He warns immigrants to be wary of requests for payment through Venmo, Zelle, or Cash App, and recommends verifying anyone offering legal services online before providing money.
